newsitem.title: USA: Garden Ridge sees inventory shortage hurting Q4.
newsitem.headline: Garden Ridge sees inventory shortage hurting Q4.

text.p: Garden Ridge Corp said the company will recognize an inventory shortage of about $2.4 million for the fiscal year ended January 26, 1997, which is expected to impact fourth quarter earnings by $.08 per share. Final audited financial results for the company will be reported on March 12, 1997.

"Although we are just beginning our fiscal 1997 year end audit, preliminary information revealed an inventory shortage at the distribution center in Dallas, which is operated under a third party arrangement, said Armand Shapiro, chairman and chief executive.
"In addition, product damage and inventory shrinkage above historical reserve levels at our retail stores contributed to the inventory shortfall."

Shapiro said the inventory shortage is not a result of markdowns nor a write-down of obsolete or excess inventory. He said the company discovered the shortage in its annual physical inventory and is in the process of working with its auditors to analyze and determine the actual shortage amount. "We will
provide additional information regarding our actual inventory results with our report of audited financial results on March 12, 1997," Shapiro said.
